blocks.orig: Listen to the rumbling of the galloping wildebeest, the roar of the lions and the laughter of the hyenas. Feel the goosebumps creep up as enormous elephant herds pass your jeep, cheetahs speed up to catch their prey, and a leopard prowls through the high grass. And don’t hold back your tears of joy when you suddenly realise how lucky you are to experience all of these wonders yourself.
blocks.html: Hear the thunder of wildebeest on the run, lions roaring and hyenas laughing. Feel the goosebumps rise as huge herds of elephants walk past your jeep, a cheetah accelerates after its prey and a leopard slinks through the tall grass. And when it suddenly dawns on you how lucky you are to see all these wonders with your own eyes, don’t hold back the tears of joy.

blocks.orig: The Serengeti is Africa’s Leading National Park 2025, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and a stage for numerous movies and documentaries. It gets its name from the Maasai language and means ‘endless plains’ – an accurate description. With its nearly 15,000 km² (6,000 sq miles), Serengeti National Park is the second-largest park in Tanzania.
blocks.html: Named Africa’s Leading National Park 2025, the Serengeti is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the backdrop to countless films and documentaries. Its name comes from the Maasai language and translates as ‘endless plains’ – which describes it well. Covering almost 15,000 km² (6,000 sq miles), Serengeti National Park ranks as Tanzania’s second-largest park.

blocks.orig: It’s home to almost all the famous African animals, including the Big Five and rare species like the African wild dog or the pangolin. The Serengeti is a place of unrivaled diversity, with striking acacia trees dotted throughout the savanna and everything from grasslands and mountains to lakes and swamps. No matter if the popular Northern Circuit, the Central Serengeti or the Western Corridor – each corner of this special speck of land holds its wonders.
blocks.html: Nearly all of Africa’s famous animals live here, the Big Five included, as well as rare species such as the pangolin and the African wild dog. The Serengeti offers diversity like nowhere else: eye-catching acacia trees scattered across the savanna, and a landscape that ranges from grasslands and mountains to swamps and lakes. Whether you choose the popular Northern Circuit, the Central Serengeti or the Western Corridor, every part of this special patch of land has its own wonders.

blocks.orig: These two unique highlights add an extra portion of wow moments and emotions to your Serengeti safari.
blocks.html: On a Serengeti safari, these two distinctive highlights bring you even more emotions and moments of awe.

blocks.orig: Every year, millions of wildebeests, zebras, and gazelles make their way to greener pastures. What sounds like a walk in the park is in fact one of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World, studded with moments of danger, excitement, and joy. On their journey, the mammals have to cross the Mara and Grumeti River with their giant crocodiles and gushing waters. All while constantly trying to outsmart hungry predators. And then there is the calving season, when several thousand babies are born every day.
blocks.html: Each year, millions of zebras, gazelles and wildebeests head for greener grazing. It may sound like a gentle stroll, but it is actually one of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World, full of danger, excitement and joy along the way. During their journey the animals must get across the Grumeti and Mara Rivers, with their rushing waters and huge crocodiles, while all the time trying to stay one step ahead of hungry predators. Then comes the calving season, when thousands of young are born every single day.

blocks.orig: The best thing: you can see this spectacle any time of the year, since the animals migrate in a circle between the Serengeti and Masai Mara (Kenya). The exact timing depends upon the rainfall patterns, which change every year.
blocks.html: Best of all, this spectacle can be seen at any point in the year, because the animals move in a loop between the Masai Mara (Kenya) and the Serengeti. Exactly when they pass depends on the rainfall, which varies from year to year.

blocks.orig: If you’re an adrenaline junkie, the river crossings are for you. They take place between June and September. While the crossing of the Grumeti River in the Western Corridor is less popular but still spectacular, the crossing of the Mara River is considered to be the “main event” of the Northern Serengeti – big audience included.
blocks.html: Love an adrenaline rush? Then the river crossings are what you’re after. They happen from June to September. The Grumeti River crossing in the Western Corridor draws fewer visitors yet is still spectacular, while the Mara River crossing is seen as the Northern Serengeti’s “main event” – complete with a large audience.

blocks.orig: Between January and March, the herds are in the Southern Serengeti and Ndutu plains. In February, around 8,000 wildebeest are born daily. This also means that many lions, cheetahs, and leopards are around for easier prey.
blocks.html: From January to March, the herds gather on the Ndutu plains and in the Southern Serengeti. Around 8,000 wildebeest are born each day in February, which also brings plenty of leopards, cheetahs and lions looking for an easier meal.

blocks.orig: From November to May, the rain transforms the Serengeti into an emerald paradise. The air is clearer, the colours more vibrant and migratory birds return in November. The perfect time for photographers looking for that perfect shot. Together with a dedicated itinerary, your chances for this one are pretty high.
blocks.html: Between November and May, the rains turn the Serengeti into a green paradise. Colours are brighter, the air is clearer, and in November the migratory birds come back. It is an ideal time for photographers hunting for that one perfect shot. Combine it with a specially designed itinerary and your odds of getting it are good.

blocks.orig:
Whenever you choose to visit the Serengeti for the migration, you will not leave disappointed. Any time is filled with unique moments which will leave you in awe.
If you want to find out more about this unique spectacle, head to our dedicated page on the Great Wildebeest Migration.
blocks.html:
Whatever time of year you pick for a Serengeti migration visit, you won’t go home disappointed. Every season brings its own special moments that will leave you amazed.
To learn more about this extraordinary spectacle, take a look at our page about the Great Wildebeest Migration.

blocks.orig: Finally, we talk about the world’s most famous group of animals: the Big Five. And yes, you can encounter all of them here. Contrary to common belief, they are not called the Big Five because they are the most majestic animals of them all. They actually got their name from big game hunters since they were the hardest animals to track down. The more you know 😉
blocks.html: Last but not least, the most famous group of animals on the planet: the Big Five. And yes, every one of them can be seen here. Despite what many people think, the name has nothing to do with them being the grandest animals of all. It actually comes from big game hunters, because these were the toughest animals to track down. The more you know 😉

blocks.orig: Let’s take a closer look at these five superstars of the Serengeti.
blocks.html: Here is a closer look at the Serengeti’s five superstars.

blocks.orig: The undisputed king of the savanna and star of The Lion King. Often found on so-called Simba Kopjes, granite outcroppings, where they do what cats do best: sleep. In the Serengeti you find big prides of lions with their offspring playing just like your kitty at home.
blocks.html: The star of The Lion King and the unchallenged king of the savanna. You’ll often spot them on the granite outcrops known as Simba Kopjes, doing what cats are best at: sleeping. The Serengeti has large prides of lions, whose cubs play just like your cat does at home.

blocks.orig: The grey and mostly gentle giants are difficult to overlook but actually difficult to hear. Despite their size, elephants move surprisingly quietly, especially through the Lobo Valley. While the largest bull of the herd seems to be the leader, the true power and wisdom of the herd lie with the oldest female.
blocks.html: These grey, mostly gentle giants are hard to miss yet surprisingly hard to hear. For all their size, elephants move remarkably quietly, particularly through the Lobo Valley. The herd’s biggest bull may look like the leader, but the real power and wisdom rest with the oldest female.

blocks.orig: Just like lions, leopards are typical cats. They like to sleep, preferably in trees, where they can hide like Houdini. The difference from cheetahs: they have rosettes instead of spots, and they are way heavier. Sometimes they let themselves simply drop from a tree to catch their prey.
blocks.html: Leopards are classic cats, just like lions. They enjoy sleeping, ideally up in trees, where they can vanish like Houdini. How they differ from cheetahs: they carry rosettes rather than spots, and they are far heavier. Now and then they simply drop out of a tree to catch their prey.

blocks.orig: Strictly speaking, only the black rhino is part of the Big Five, not the white rhino (apparently they were easier to hunt). While white rhinos have a wide lip, black rhinos have a pointed one. Their colour has nothing to do with their name: it’s probably a mistranslation of the Afrikaans/Dutch word wyd (meaning “wide”), referring to its broad lip, which English speakers misinterpreted as the colour “white”. They then named the other species “black” simply as a contrast.
blocks.html: Technically, the Big Five includes only the black rhino and not the white rhino (which was apparently easier to hunt). The white rhino has a broad lip, whereas the black rhino’s is pointed. The names have nothing to do with colour: most likely “white” is a mistranslation of the Afrikaans/Dutch word wyd (meaning “wide”), describing its broad lip, which English speakers took to mean the colour. The other species was then called “black” just to contrast with it.

blocks.orig: According to the novelist and safari enthusiast Ernest Hemingway, the African buffalo “looks at you as if you owe him money.” It’s quite fitting, actually: the animal is considered one of the most dangerous of the Big Five because they are famously short-tempered. Also, they would beat anyone in a staring contest.
blocks.html: Ernest Hemingway, novelist and safari lover, said the African buffalo “looks at you as if you owe him money.” That is rather apt: famously short-tempered, it is regarded as one of the most dangerous members of the Big Five. It would also win any staring contest.

blocks.orig: With so many adventures awaiting you during a Serengeti safari, you need to rest well and in style. After all, nothing beats a good night’s sleep surrounded by the sounds of the savanna.
blocks.html: A Serengeti safari is full of adventure, so you need to rest well and in comfort. After all, there is nothing better than a good night’s sleep with the sounds of the savanna all around you.

Below you’ll find a few frequently asked questions, plus links to pages with more detail. If your question isn’t answered here, you are always welcome to contact our safari experts.

blocks.orig: This depends on what you want to see. During the dry season (June to October and December to February) you can spot wildlife easier since they gather around waterholes more often. Also, the weather is more pleasant. The downside: it’s peak season with more tourists and higher hotel prices.
blocks.html: It depends on what you’d like to see. In the dry season (June to October and December to February), wildlife is easier to spot because the animals gather at waterholes more often, and the weather is nicer too. The drawback: it is peak season, so there are more tourists and hotel prices are higher.

blocks.orig: The mid season from March to November offers a balance of moderate hotel rates and fewer tourists. The weather can be variable, and some attractions might have limited availability (due to rains), but you still get great wildlife sightings and a more relaxed safari experience.
blocks.html: From March to November, the mid season gives you a good balance of fewer visitors and moderate hotel rates. The weather can change, and because of the rains some attractions may have limited availability, but the wildlife sightings are still excellent and the safari feels more relaxed.

blocks.orig: The wet season in April and May is perfect for budget-conscious travelers since the hotel rates are the lowest. The heavy rains make the scenery vibrant and lush, but travel plans can be affected by the weather.
blocks.html: If you’re watching your budget, the wet season in April and May is ideal, as hotel rates are at their lowest. The heavy rains turn the landscape lush and vivid, though the weather can disrupt travel plans.

blocks.orig: More details about the ideal travel time can be found here.
blocks.html: You’ll find more information on the best time to travel on this page.

blocks.orig: Due to its sheer size, you should spend at least two days to get into the Serengeti feeling. Even if it might feel a bit rushed, you get to see the highlights and hopefully all the Big Five.
blocks.html: Because the park is so large, plan at least two days to really get a feel for the Serengeti. It may feel a little hurried, but you’ll see the highlights and, with luck, all of the Big Five.

blocks.orig: Three to four days is ideal to explore the Central Serengeti and one other seasonal region, like the North for river crossings or the South for calving.
blocks.html: Ideally, take three to four days so you can explore the Central Serengeti plus one other seasonal area, such as the South for the calving or the North for the river crossings.

blocks.orig: If you can spend five to seven days, you have time for the perfect picture or to wait for a specific hunt or a river crossing to happen.
blocks.html: With five to seven days, you can take your time to get the perfect photo or wait for a particular hunt or river crossing.

blocks.orig: No matter how much time you have, we’ll plan your Serengeti route in such a way that it gives you the best possible experience.

blocks.html: Rather not go on safari alone? Then you can join our 5-day group trip, which spends two days in the Serengeti. In the calving season the trip also visits Ndutu, where you can watch new life arriving in the world.

blocks.orig: Not only can you witness the wonders of African nature, but you can also make new friends for life. A classic win-win situation.
blocks.html: You get to see the wonders of African nature and may well make friends for life along the way. A true win-win.

blocks.html: We collect travellers from their hotel in Arusha on the first Wednesday of each month. More information is available on this page.

blocks.orig: First things first: no, you don’t have to dress like a ranger. However, neutral colours are definitely more advisable than neon pink or bright yellow.
blocks.html: To start with: no, there is no need to dress like a ranger. That said, neutral colours are a much better choice than bright yellow or neon pink.

blocks.orig: Next to t-shirts or tanktops, make sure to also bring a sweater or a jacket since the mornings and evenings can be quite cold.
blocks.html: Along with t-shirts or tank tops, pack a jacket or a sweater, as it can get fairly cold in the mornings and evenings.

blocks.orig: Shorts are absolute must-haves, but you can also switch them for light long trousers or convertible zip-off trousers.
blocks.html: Shorts are essential, though you can swap them for convertible zip-off trousers or light long trousers.

blocks.orig: A bandana or a hat is advisable – the sun can be fierce. And of course sunscreen, sunglasses and insect repellent.
blocks.html: A hat or a bandana is a good idea, as the sun can be strong. Don’t forget sunglasses, insect repellent and sunscreen either.

blocks.orig: To capture all these unique moments, have your camera close and switched on!
blocks.html: Keep your camera switched on and within reach so you can capture all these special moments!
